# BrutalKit: Full AI and LLM Reference

## 1. Project identity

BrutalKit is a lightweight, dependency-free, CSS-first Neo-Brutalist component library in `ravvdevv/brutal-kit`. It provides reusable primitives without requiring React, Vue, Svelte, or another framework. Frameworks can consume its classes normally.

Do not turn it into a framework, add a runtime dependency for styling, or introduce a global reset.

## 2. Source-of-truth map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/brutal.css` | Authoritative component CSS and design tokens |
| `src/brutal.js` | Optional browser interactions: tabs and dialogs |
| `dist/brutal.css` | Generated distributable CSS |
| `dist/brutal.min.css` | Generated minified CSS |
| `scripts/build.mjs` | CSS build pipeline |
| `components.json` | Machine-readable public component inventory |
| `schemas/components.schema.json` | Manifest JSON Schema |
| `docs/architecture.md` | Runtime boundaries and performance policy |
| `docs/recipes.md` | Copyable semantic integration recipes |
| `tests/` | Regression coverage |
| `docs.html` | Human-readable documentation |
| `AGENTS.md` | Required coding-agent instructions |

Never hand-edit generated `dist/`. Edit source, run the build, and commit generated output with the source change.

## 3. Design principles

- Use clear geometry, deliberate borders, hard offset shadows, restrained bright accents, and strong typography.
- Prefer legibility and hierarchy over decoration.
- Reuse design tokens. Avoid arbitrary one-off colors and values.
- Avoid gratuitous gradients, glassmorphism, neon, excessive rounding, random animation, ornamental dashboards, and decorative UI without purpose.
- Respect consuming applications. No broad selectors or global reset.

## 4. Design tokens

The visual direction follows Cramio's design system: paper `#f7f6f2`, ink navy `#20233b`, purple primary `#7055d9`, amber `#ffc93c`, sky `#a7c8ff`, peach `#ffab7e`, mint `#9ff0c2`, and lilac `#cfc7ff`. The default type pairing is DM Sans for body copy and Manrope for display headings, with system fallbacks. Components use 10px default radii and offset ink shadows.

Current public tokens include `--bk-bg`, `--bk-surface`, `--bk-ink`, `--bk-muted`, `--bk-purple`, `--bk-purple-dark`, `--bk-yellow`, `--bk-blue`, `--bk-pink`, `--bk-success`, `--bk-danger`, `--bk-lilac`, `--bk-border-width`, `--bk-border`, `--bk-shadow`, `--bk-shadow-sm`, `--bk-radius`, `--bk-font`, and `--bk-font-display`. Inspect `src/brutal.css` for exact values.

Consumers may override custom properties without forking the source. Layout utilities support local `--bk-stack-gap`, `--bk-row-gap`, and `--bk-grid-gap`.

## 5. Component API

The machine-readable inventory in `components.json` is the canonical index of public classes, data attributes, JS requirements, semantics, and keyboard contracts. Verify the source before relying on any API.

Categories include buttons, cards, badges, form controls, alerts, layout utilities, tabs, native disclosure accordions, native dialogs, tooltips, and visually-hidden accessibility utility.

Do not invent classes, modifiers, props, or runtime APIs. This is an HTML/CSS library, not a React component package.

## 6. CSS integration

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ravvdevv/brutal-kit@main/dist/brutal.min.css">
```

The `@main` URL is mutable. Pin a published immutable version tag when available. Do not claim npm installation: current package metadata is a private development workspace and no npm publication is established.

BrutalKit intentionally does not apply a global box-sizing reset or broad element styling.

## 7. Optional JavaScript

CSS works independently. The optional module currently enhances tabs and native `dialog` elements.

```js
import { initBrutalKit } from "./src/brutal.js";
initBrutalKit(document.querySelector("#app"));
```

Importing in a browser auto-initializes `document`. Call `initBrutalKit(root)` for a separately mounted root. The initializer avoids duplicate setup on the same root.

### Tabs

- Tablist: `[data-bk-tabs][role="tablist"]`.
- Tabs: `[role="tab"]` with `aria-controls` pointing to a panel.
- Panels: `[role="tabpanel"]` with `aria-labelledby` pointing to the tab.
- Exactly one enabled tab should be selected.
- Arrow keys wrap through enabled tabs; Home/End move to first/last.
- Use `aria-orientation="vertical"` for vertical tablists.
- Inactive panels use the native `hidden` attribute.

### Dialog

- Use native `<dialog data-bk-dialog>`.
- Open with `data-bk-dialog-open="dialog-id"`.
- Close from inside with `data-bk-dialog-close`.
- Give the dialog an accessible name, usually via `aria-labelledby`.
- Native dialog supplies modal behavior and Escape-to-close; BrutalKit restores focus to the opener.
- Include a visible close/cancel action.

Accordions use native `<details>` / `<summary>`. Tooltips are supplementary; essential content must remain available outside them.

## 8. Accessibility

Use semantic HTML and native controls. Label every input, provide accessible names for icon-only controls, preserve visible focus, honor reduced motion, and do not use color as the only status indicator. Do not claim WCAG conformance just because the library has focus styles. Test the composed application.

## 9. Architecture and performance

- No runtime dependencies. Prefer browser-native APIs.
- Do not load JavaScript for CSS-only components.
- Avoid polling, layout thrashing, global observers, and per-element listeners when event delegation works.
- Keep selectors scoped to library classes/data attributes.
- Keep optional JS small.
- Do not add framework wrappers or component registry runtimes.
- See `docs/architecture.md` for boundaries and component change workflow.

CI enforces these conservative file-size ceilings: 9 KiB minified CSS, 12 KiB readable CSS, and 5 KiB optional JS. They are raw file-size guardrails, not gzip/brotli transfer measurements. Raise them only with measured justification.

## 10. Agent workflow

Before editing:
1. Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, this guide, and relevant docs.
2. Inspect `components.json`, actual source, and tests.
3. Decide whether a change belongs in library source, generated output, demo site, or documentation.
4. Prefer the smallest coherent change.

While editing:
1. Preserve the CSS-first, framework-agnostic contract.
2. Avoid new dependencies without a demonstrated need.
3. Keep changes focused and modular.
4. Never invent npm commands, versions, CDN paths, or APIs.
5. Regenerate `dist/` through the build script.
6. Keep examples semantic, accessible, and copyable.
7. Never add controls that do nothing.

Before finishing:
1. Run `bun run build`, `bun run test`, `bun run check:manifest`, and `bun run check:size`.
2. Review `git diff --check` and the full diff.
3. Verify metadata, docs, source, and generated CSS are consistent.
4. Report changed files, actual commands/results, and unperformed checks.
5. Never claim browser QA, deployment, or accessibility audits unless performed.
